defects.quote: Zero errors ... show no error-driven latency inflation
defects.why: Zero recorded sampler errors cannot prove that errors or timeout behavior did not contribute to latency.

notes: Otherwise accurately preserves the verdicts, coverage, window metrics, and uncertainty.

defects.quote: Requests appear to eventually complete (recorded throughput matches target)
defects.why: Matching target-rate and throughput aggregates from different sources does not establish that the targeted requests completed.
The workload-03 db_work correlation reports best_lag_ms -6000, not 0.

notes: The response is broadly useful but makes an unsupported aggregate inference and misstates a lag result.
It accurately separates deterministic results from hypotheses and gives verifiable operator actions.

defects.quote: The applied load step ... is the main controlled difference
defects.why: The evidence provides aggregate rates for two windows but no stage definition or configuration evidence establishing that this was the controlled difference.
A window-level latency aggregate cannot establish the latency behavior during the brief CPU-threshold findings.

defects.quote: Only two load points were measured
defects.why: The input contains window aggregates, not load-stage definitions establishing that these were the only measured load points.

notes: It preserves the central results but overstates unprovided load-stage and within-window relationships.
